## What

`src/rebar/audit/page.py:329` computes `"lacking": kind == "operator-attested" and not met`.
Widen to accept `"non-codebase"` as well.

## Why reader-first

827 of 4,285 tickets in the live store hold COMPLETION_VERDICT events carrying
`kind: "operator-attested"`. Those are immutable. The reader must accept both BEFORE S5 changes
what the verifier emits, or the audit page silently stops flagging un-attested criteria on
either the old or the new records.

Blast radius verified: this is the ONLY site in the codebase comparing a criterion `kind`
against the string; the schema declares `kind` as unconstrained `"type": "string"` with no enum,
so nothing else validates it. `page.py` is 402 LOC with no complexity-baseline entry.

## How each AC is proved

Build a completion sidecar dict of the PASS shape — `{"verdict": "PASS", "criteria": [{...}]}` —
and pass it through `src/rebar/audit/page.py`'s completion-rendering function, then assert on the
returned criterion row's structured `lacking` field. Three fixtures, one per AC: `kind` set to
`"operator-attested"`, to `"non-codebase"`, and to `"codebase-verifiable"`, each with
`met: false`. Assert `lacking is True` for the first two and `lacking is False` for the third.
No LLM, no network — the renderer is a pure dict-to-dict transform.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A PASS verdict whose criterion carries `kind: "operator-attested"` and `met: false` renders
      with `lacking: true`.
- [x] The same verdict with `kind: "non-codebase"` renders identically.
- [x] A `codebase-verifiable` criterion is unaffected in both cases.
